title: Bind the prepared Claude runtime to the committed activation
description:
Objective: close the measured hole where a coherent activation for runtime A can launch pinned runtime B. Split out of task-c81953d210f14cdeb9f6070a443b6750 (see comment-31ffc39112a54993987f4363e33584e5 there) because that task's rail 1 forbids changing default launchClaude behavior, its written DoD does not name this guard, and this guard's blast radius is a separate test/fixture surgery.

MEASURED GAP at HEAD 0371ead (commands run, results recorded):
- `grep -n runtimeObservationDigest packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-kernel.ts` -> line 196: `EffectIntent.runtimeObservationDigest: string` EXISTS.
- `packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-activation.ts:215-217` already compares `request.observedRuntimeDigest !== intent.runtimeObservationDigest` and refuses `PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED` with leg `runtimeObservation`. That is the AUTHORITATIVE mapping to preserve; do not mint a new code.
- `validateActivationCommit` (packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-grant.ts:110-148) checks intent/attempt states, attempt<->intent binding, grant<->intent binding and grantId derivation ONLY. It never reads `runtimeObservationDigest`. Its `CommitCheck` returns `{kind:"COHERENT", ok:true, activationDigest}` and nothing else.
- `decodeCommit` (claude-launcher-port-results.ts:201-208) therefore yields only `activationDigest: string`.
- `prepareClaudeRuntimePin` yields `quotedObservationDigest`, `freshObservationDigest`, `bindingDigest` (decodeRuntime, claude-launcher-port-results.ts:173-199).
- `grep -rn "runtimeObservationDigest" packages/runner/src/providers/` -> ZERO hits. launchClaude never compares the two. Gap is real and open.

FIXTURE BLAST RADIUS (measured, plan for it): `claude-launcher-test-fixtures.ts` builds `COMMIT` at module scope from `makeActivationRequest()` whose `runtimeObservationDigest` is `DIGEST.runtime` (effect-test-fixtures.ts:83), while `prepared` is built in `beforeAll` from a real temp executable. The two digests differ today, so a naive guard reddens most of claude-launcher.test.ts. The fixture must be restructured so the activation commit is derived from the SAME prepared runtime observation, or the guard must take the quoted observation digest the intent was built from.

Deliverable: an exact comparison in the launcher at the ACTIVATION phase, strictly before the grant phase and before any physical open, refusing with the authoritative `PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED` code at its authoritative layer when the prepared runtime does not match the committed `EffectIntent.runtimeObservationDigest`.

NOT in scope: the authority-port overlay (task-c81953d210f14cdeb9f6070a443b6750 owns it), daemon persistence, schema, ingress.

Hard dependencies: none. May land in parallel with task-c81953d210f14cdeb9f6070a443b6750; both are prerequisites of task-996e5318c3a64caa9f5eb661ace927a3 and task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9.
definitionOfDone: The launcher compares the prepared runtime observation against the committed EffectIntent.runtimeObservationDigest at the ACTIVATION phase, strictly after validateCommit succeeds and strictly before the grant phase, the OS lock, and openBoundary.

A drifted runtime refuses with the authoritative PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED code and the layer effect-activation.ts already uses for that refusal; no new error code is minted, and the refusal echoes no runtime path, grant id, or bootstrap credential digest.

A matching runtime still launches: the existing launcher happy-path and duplicate-delivery behaviour is unchanged, and the fixture is restructured so its activation commit and its prepared runtime carry the same observation digest rather than the guard being weakened to accommodate the fixture.

Tests assert the exact code AND that the ACTIVATION layer answered, assert zero calls to consumeGrant, acquireLock and openBoundary on drift, and a mutation drill flipping the comparison operand or deleting the guard reddens a named outcome assertion (not only a shape assertion).

Focused @moe/runner typecheck and tests pass; repo-wide legs are recorded as a merge-base-vs-HEAD path-attributed baseline; no production file in packages/runner/src/providers/claude exceeds 250 physical lines.
taskRails: Preserve the authoritative PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED mapping and layer from packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-activation.ts; do not mint a launcher-local code for runtime drift and do not reimplement the comparison the supervisor already owns if it can be composed.
Use TDD. The drift test must pin the exact code and the exact layer, and must prove which layer answered, because validateCommit can also refuse at ACTIVATION with ACTIVATION_COMMIT_INCOHERENT.
Do not weaken or narrow the guard to make the existing fixture pass; fix the fixture so the committed intent and the prepared runtime share one observation digest.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source, split before 400. No daemon or store code in this runner task.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) A BARE `!==` IN THE LAUNCHER, comparing a runtimeObservationDigest threaded out through CommitCheck — REJECTED by task rail 1. It is a second copy of a comparison the supervisor owns, and the two copies can drift silently: the launcher's copy would keep passing after someone changed the activation-side code or layer. Extracting one shared helper makes drill D1 redden BOTH suites from a single edit, which is the only mechanical proof the two sites agree.

2) INJECT THE BINDING CHECK AS A NEW LAUNCHER PORT — REJECTED. `snapshotLauncherPorts` requires every PORT_KEYS entry, so a new key silently refuses every existing full-`deps` caller, and port-results.ts has no line headroom. The check is pure, so injection buys nothing but a hostile-result decoder nobody needs.

3) COMPARE `freshObservationDigest` — REJECTED as measured-wrong. It digests the PINNED closure whose paths live under the pin root, so it can never equal the quote and would refuse every correct launch. See codebaseInsights.

4) EXPRESS THE DRIFT FIXTURE BY MUTATING THE INTENT'S runtimeObservationDigest — REJECTED, and this is task rail 2's trap. `deriveGrantId` covers the intent, so any intent mutation makes `validateActivationCommit` refuse ACTIVATION_COMMIT_INCOHERENT at the SAME layer FIRST, and the new guard would never execute while the test still looked green. The drift fixture must instead be a fully COHERENT activation built with the default `DIGEST.runtime` whose digest simply differs from the real prepared runtime — which is exactly today's fixture, so drift is the cheaper fixture and MATCH is the one that needs construction.

5) WEAKEN THE GUARD TO ACCEPT THE EXISTING FIXTURE (e.g. compare only when both are present) — REJECTED by task rail 3 and by the epic's fail-closed rail. The fixture is what changes.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
ARCHITECT MEASUREMENT at HEAD 0371ead — commands run and what they returned.

GAP STILL OPEN: `grep -rn "runtimeObservationDigest" packages/runner/src/providers/` -> ZERO hits. The launcher never compares the prepared runtime to the committed intent.

AUTHORITATIVE MAPPING (effect-activation.ts:213-218, read verbatim): `if (request.observedRuntimeDigest !== intent.runtimeObservationDigest) return refuse("PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED", "runtime observation digest does not match the quote", "runtimeObservation")`. `refuse` (line 77-79) is `grantRefusal(code, leg === null ? "KERNEL" : "ACTIVATION", message, leg)`, so the authoritative triple is code PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED, layer ACTIVATION, leg runtimeObservation. The comment directly above it already says "the wrapper resolves the runtime closure and compares it to the quote-bound observation" — the launcher is the intended second enforcement point, so this task finishes a design-798 intent rather than inventing policy.

WHICH PREPARED DIGEST IS THE RIGHT OPERAND — this is the one thing a worker will get wrong. It is `quotedObservationDigest`, NOT `freshObservationDigest`.
- claude-runtime-pin.ts:187 `const quote = readQuote(request.quotedObservation)`, then :219 `pinAndBind(request, sources, quote.digest, ...)` and :245 `quotedObservationDigest` flows into the prepared record. `readQuote` (claude-runtime-pin-closure.ts:145-158) recomputes `canonicalDigest(observationDigestInput(observation))` and REFUSES unless it equals `observation.observationDigest`. So `prepared.quotedObservationDigest` is exactly the self-covering digest of the observation the caller quoted — the same value a daemon would have committed into `EffectIntent.runtimeObservationDigest`.
- `freshObservationDigest` is `observation.observationDigest` of the RE-OBSERVED PINNED closure (claude-runtime-pin.ts:155). Its closure entries carry paths under the pin root, so it can never equal the installed-root quote by construction. Comparing it would refuse every correct launch. quoted<->fresh equivalence is already proven inside the pin by `authorityDigest` (:213) and `factsDigest` (:283), which are path-independent.

COMPOSABILITY: `revalidate()` in effect-activation.ts is private and performs eight other checks over a full activation request, so it cannot be called from the launcher. But the single comparison CAN be extracted so both sites share one copy — that is what task rail 1 asks for. Both `ActivationOutcome`'s and `CommitCheck`'s REFUSED arms are the same `{kind:"REFUSED", failure: SupervisorFailure}` shape produced by `grantRefusal`, so one helper returning `refusal | null` serves both callers with no adapter.

WHY NOT A NEW LAUNCHER PORT: adding a key to PORT_KEYS (claude-launcher-port-results.ts:44) would make `snapshotLauncherPorts` reject every existing caller that hands a full `deps` object, and that file is EXACTLY 250 physical lines. `validateRuntimeBinding` is pure and deterministic, so a direct import needs only throw-containment, not hostile-result decoding.

- `makeActivationRequest(overrides)` and `makeIntent(overrides)` are both already exported from effect-test-fixtures.ts and accept `unknown`-typed overrides, so the matched activation is `makeActivationRequest({ intent: makeIntent({ runtimeObservationDigest: observation.observationDigest }), observedRuntimeDigest: observation.observationDigest })`. NO edit to effect-test-fixtures.ts is required — it is shared by 14 files and must not be touched.
- Every `COMMIT` reference in claude-launcher.test.ts (lines 163, 219, 224, 225) is INSIDE an `it(...)` body, never in a `describe` body, so moving COMMIT construction into `beforeAll` cannot break collection. The fixture already uses the `export let ... ; beforeAll(...)` pattern for `runtimeRequest` and `prepared` — follow it.
- `claude-launcher-test-fixtures.ts` is imported by claude-launcher.test.ts ONLY.
- The pre-open refusal table at claude-launcher.test.ts:222-231 already asserts `cases.length).toBe(8)`, `log` not containing "open", empty `boundary.log`, exact code/layer, and `ran === cases.length`. Adding the drift case means bumping 8 to 9 — the epic's generated-case rail makes that bump mandatory, not optional.
- On drift the fixture `log` should be EXACTLY `["runtime","validate"]`. That exact-equality assertion is the ordering proof and is far more mutation-sensitive than `not.toContain("open")`.

planningNotes.risks:
LAYERED REFUSAL (the defect this task is most likely to ship)
- `validateActivationCommit` also refuses at layer ACTIVATION. Layer alone cannot tell the two apart — the drift test MUST pin code PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED, and drill D2 (delete only the launcher guard, leave the supervisor helper intact) is what proves the launcher-side enforcement is separately tested rather than answered by validateCommit.

- Conversely, drill D1 (break the shared helper) must redden BOTH suites. If it reddens only one, the extraction did not actually become the single source and rail 1 is unmet.

FIXTURE POSITIVE CONTROL
- A matched fixture that is not really matched, plus a dead guard, is indistinguishable from a working guard. Drill D5 reverts the matched commit to `DIGEST.runtime` and requires the OBSERVED happy-path test to redden. Without D5 the whole task can ship green and enforce nothing.

ORDERING
- DoD 1 requires the guard strictly before grant, lock and open. Assert the fixture `log` EQUALS `["runtime","validate"]` on drift — not merely that it lacks "open" — and drill D4 by moving the guard after the grant phase; the exact-equality assertion must redden.

CONTAINMENT
- `validateRuntimeBinding` is called directly, not through a port, so nothing else catches a throw. Wrap the call in try/catch and map a throw to CLAUDE_LAUNCH_DEPENDENCY_THROWN at ACTIVATION, or a hostile `request.effect` could reject launchClaude's public promise and break the landed total-result containment. `snapshotClaudeLaunchRequest` has already bounded `request.effect` to plain data by that point, so this is belt-and-braces, but the launcher's containment invariant is absolute.

MESSAGE HYGIENE
- Do NOT reuse PHASE.activation ("the activation-commit authority did not answer usably") for this refusal — it names the wrong authority. Add a distinct PHASE entry. The message must not contain the runtime path, either digest, the grant id, or the bootstrap credential digest; the supervisor's own message already models this ("runtime observation digest does not match the quote" — no operands).

The edits are in different regions and this task changes no fixture SIGNATURE (`request()`, `dependencies()`, `boundaryHarness()`, `failureOf()` keep their shapes), so both can land.
